logline: A worker bee asks why the giant who keeps stealing her hive's honey plants flowers every time; the flowers spread until she gets lost, she flies up to find home, and the meadow is a giant bee with her hive as its heart.
question: why does the giant plant flowers every time he steals the honey?
premise: A lone beehive on the High Meadow. A giant (a player) has taken its honey 52 times: he lights a campfire under it so the bees stay calm, bottles the honey, then plants a row of flowers. The narrator, a worker bee, thinks he feels bad about stealing. He tells the bees they're his favorite; she's sure he means the honey. He plants pink around the hive (so they can find home, she thinks). The field keeps growing, the bees fly farther every day, and today she flew so far she couldn't see home.
twist: He isn't paying for the honey: he's drawing them. One row per bottle, 52 rows, the meadow is one huge bee seen from above, and the pink heart around the hive is its heart. 'You're my FAVORITE' meant the bees. Said by the bee over the top-down picture: 'all the flowers made one giant BEE, with HOME right in its HEART'.
payoff_note: `top`: the stunt mark when the rising camera settles straight down over the whole bee (S10), by L11's BEE. L11 (the reveal) is said over it, L12 (the sting, echoing line 1's 52) over the hold; the Short ends 1.0 s after L12.

[A friendly teenage boy, bright and goofy]

lines.text: In my world, / a GIANT / steals our honey, / and plants FLOWERS. / Fifty-two TIMES. / WHY?
lines.say: In my world, a giant steals our honey, and plants flowers. Fifty-two times. Why?
lines.direction: a bubbly complaint, like telling on him; one breath, the WHY bright and baffled, up

lines.text: First, SMOKE. / Me and my SISTERS / go all SLEEPY. / We HATE that.
lines.say: First, smoke. Me and my sisters go all sleepy. We hate that.

lines.text: Then CLINK, / honey GONE. / One BOTTLE, / one ROW / of FLOWERS.
lines.say: Then clink, honey gone. One bottle, one row of flowers.
lines.direction: quick and matter-of-fact, counting it off
a little sorry for him, sure of it
bright and goofy, grinning at a tiny bee

lines.text: He plants PINK ones / around our DOOR, / so we can / find HOME. / Like we'd EVER / get LOST.
lines.say: He plants pink ones around our door, so we can find home. Like we'd ever get lost.
lines.direction: amused, a bit superior, the last word up

lines.text: But now / the flowers / never END. / I HAD to know WHY. / So I went / to find / the EDGE.
lines.say: But now the flowers never end. I had to know why. So I went to find the edge.
lines.direction: determined and bright, off on an adventure; 'I HAD to know WHY' is the viewer's question, said for them

lines.text: I flew / SO far, / I couldn't see HOME. / Or my SISTERS.
lines.say: I flew so far, I couldn't see home. Or my sisters.
lines.direction: surprised at herself, a small wobble on SISTERS, still bright (never scared before the reveal)

lines.text: So I flew / UP, / UP, / UP, / to find them.
lines.say: So I flew up, up, up, to find them.
lines.direction: brave and bouncy, each UP higher; the crane lifts on the first UP

lines.text: And ALL the flowers / made one / giant BEE. / With HOME / right in its HEART.
lines.say: And all the flowers made one giant bee. With home right in its heart.
lines.direction: the reveal, plain and amazed, slower: she says what she sees; BEE lands as the camera settles
the sting, soft and wondering, counting; echoes line 1's FIFTY-TWO; cut ~1 s after ROWS
